east_text: Strength is of weakness oft the spoil; The store in ruins mocks our toil.
west_text: Our strength grows out of our weakness.

east_text: (Thus) I alone am different from other men, but I value the nursing-mother (the Tao).
west_text: Whoso would be a man, must be a nonconformist.

east_text: He diminishes it and again diminishes it, till he arrives at doing nothing (on purpose).
west_source: Thoreau, Walden — Where I Lived, and What I Lived For
west_text: Instead of three meals a day, if it be necessary eat but one; instead of a hundred dishes, five; and reduce other things in proportion.

east_text: Therefore the sufficiency of contentment is an enduring and unchanging sufficiency.
west_text: Shall we always study to obtain more of these things, and not sometimes to be content with less?

east_text: Purity and stillness give the correct law to all under heaven.
west_text: It seems as if we needed only the stillness and composed attitude of the library to seize the thought.

east_text: Purity and impurity belong to oneself, no one can purify another.
west_text: By turns our purity inspires and our impurity casts us down.

east_text: To know and yet (think) we do not know is the highest (attainment); not to know (and yet think) we do know is a disease.
west_text: It is the harder because you will always find those who think they know what is your duty better than you know it.

east_text: The soft overcomes the hard; and the weak the strong.
west_text: Every man is actually weak and apparently strong.

east_text: All things spring up, and there is not one which declines to show itself; they grow, and there is no claim made for their ownership; they go through their processes, and there is no expectation (of a reward for the results).
west_text: Thus there is no sleep, no pause, no preservation, but all things renew, germinate and spring.

east_text: This world is dark, few only can see here; a few only go to heaven, like birds escaped from the net.
west_text: Thank Heaven, here is not all the world.
